title: Adaptive headroom shedding with fidelity proxy and per-tenant soft quotas
creator: Ethan Brooks
description:
Background: During multi-region failovers and transient overloads we need a predictable, tenant-fair approach to preserve latency SLOs while maximizing useful work. Existing playbooks rely on hard token caps or coarse priority lanes which either over-evict or create noisy neighbor outcomes.

Proposal: Implement an "adaptive headroom shedding" system paired with a lightweight "fidelity proxy" layer. Key ideas: 
  1) Headroom metric: compute per-queue and per-tenant headroom as the time/throughput margin to configured latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99). Headroom drives a soft shedding probability rather than binary admission.
  2) Fidelity proxy: a runtime component that mediates admitted requests and can apply graded fidelity transformations (e.g., response truncation, reduce sampling complexity, switch to cached/sketch responses, or proxy to a cheaper model) based on per-request budget and tenant policy.
  3) Soft quotas and prioritized lanes: combine tenant soft quotas (elastic allowances that replenish with usage patterns) with priority scoring. Tenants within headroom keep full fidelity; those approaching negative headroom receive probabilistic shedding with fidelity steps.
  4) Circuit breaker integration: integrate with regional circuit breakers so fidelity proxy can trigger immediate lower-fidelity fallbacks when downstream shards are unhealthy.

Why different: This approach avoids immediate full request rejection by providing graded degradation (fidelity steps) and uses continuous headroom signals to make fair admission decisions. It ties SLO telemetry directly to shedding behavior and enables controlled multi-region failover modes where fidelity profiles differ per-region.

Scope and non-goals: Focus on request admission and runtime fidelity adjustments. Not in scope: billing changes, customer-facing quota UI (will add later), or full model-merging.

Implementation overview: 
  - Controller: headroom aggregator service (local regional replica) subscribes to latency/throughput metrics and publishes per-tenancy headroom buckets. 
  - Admission shim: admission controller reads headroom and makes probabilistic accept/reject vs accept-with-fidelity decisions. 
  - Fidelity proxy: sidecar in front of model-serving that transforms or routes accepted requests to the appropriate model or applies truncation/simpler decoding.
  - Telemetry: expose per-tenant acceptance rate, fidelity-step ratios, post-fidelity latency, and quality regressions to Console dashboards and alerts.

Design constraints and trade-offs: 
  - Safety vs utility: graded fidelity preserves utility but risks subtle quality regressions. Mitigation: link fidelity steps to automated evals and monitor cohort user signals.
  - Determinism: probabilistic shedding introduces variability; will seed RNG with tenant+window for reproducible behavior across retries.
  - Complexity: adds runtime components; start with a single fidelity proxy profile (truncate + low-temp sampling) and expand.

Rollout plan: 
  1) Simulation: run synthetic load tests on staging with traffic-replay and modelled tenant distributions. Acceptance threshold: 20% reduction in hard rejects and <=5% upstream latency SLO violation regression.
  2) Canary: enable adaptive shedding for 5% of traffic on a non-critical region, monitor fidelity loss metrics and customer error rates for 2 weeks.
  3) Gradual ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 100% for regional control planes, with ability to disable per-tenant.

Telemetry & SLO tie-ins: 
  - New SLI: headroom_seconds (per-tenancy window), acceptance_rate_by_tenant, fidelity_step_impact (quality delta), fallback_count.
  - Alerts: headroom <= 0 for >10s triggers operator paging; fidelity-step quality degradation >3% triggers rollback.

Deliverables: 
  - RFC and sequence diagrams (Confluence).
  - Headroom aggregator implementation (Go, k8s operator).
  - Admission shim library (C++) and open-source wrapper for other languages.
  - Fidelity proxy sidecar (prototype in Python, replaceable).
  - Console dashboards & runbooks.

Acceptance criteria: 
  - SLO preservation: during staged overload tests, p95 latency regressions <=5% relative to baseline.
  - Reduced hard rejects: decrease in 503-like rejections by >=15% under same load.
  - Quality guardrails: for fidelity steps, automated evals show <4% drop in task-specific metrics (BLEU/EM/embedding similarity) for top affected tenants.

Backwards compatibility: The admission shim will default to current deterministic admission if headroom data is missing; fidelity proxy is opt-in per-deployment.
acceptance_criteria: Headroom metric computed and exported for all regional queues
Admission shim can make probabilistic accept/accept-with-fidelity/reject decisions using headroom buckets
Fidelity proxy sidecar supports at least 3 degradation steps and routing to a cheaper model
Staging load tests demonstrate >=15% fewer hard rejects with p95 latency regression <=5%
Console dashboard surfaces per-tenant acceptance and fidelity-step ratios with alerting rules

comments: 2026-03-02 Ethan Brooks: Initial problem statement and early proposal posted. Requested feedback from SRE and Model Ops on fidelity guardrails.
2026-03-04 Asha Kapoor: Added proposed headroom formula and probabilistic mapping in RFC draft. Noted that per-tenant quotas should be sticky across retries.
2026-03-06 Priya Menon (SRE): Simulation config looks reasonable; requested we add failure injection (region partition) tests to validate multi-region failover behavior.
2026-03-08 David Lopez (Model Ops): Agreed to provide a lightweight 'cheap-model' docker image for staging. Raised concerns about metric tagging for tracing fidelity-induced regressions.
2026-03-10 Design review: Maria Delgado suggested showing fidelity step UX in Console (badge and impact popover) so customer success can proactively contact affected customers.
2026-03-12 Asha Kapoor: Prototype headroom aggregator is live in staging (region-us-east-1). Running first synthetic spike; see PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1284
notes: We must coordinate with legal before enabling fidelity fallbacks for regulated tenants. Ops should be able to pin tenants to 'no-fidelity' mode. Next sync with Model Ops scheduled for 2026-03-15.
